interest: Illuminates Cold War struggles over the Orthodox Church and Asian objections to American promotion of Christian proselytization.
overview: This file contains U.S. State Department correspondence, intelligence despatches, and SCAP records from 1945 to 1949 concerning religious affairs in occupied Japan. Key topics include the disestablishment of State Shinto, guarantees of religious freedom, the wartime conditions and postwar revival of Christian denominations, Catholic property and educational requests, and the political attitudes of Buddhist and Communist groups. The records also document significant Cold War geopolitical friction surrounding Soviet attempts to control the Japanese Orthodox Church, as well as diplomatic protests from Indian and Burmese organizations objecting to perceived Allied favoritism toward Christian proselytization.
